results.title: Artificial intelligence in science: Overview and policy ...
results.content: Such applications include, among others, AI and collective intelligence, AI and laboratory robotics, AI and citizen science, developments in scientific fact-checking, and the emerging uses of AI in research governance. * Consider the implications of AI in science for developing countries, and the measures that could be taken to expedite uptake in developing-country research. One of its most significant offerings is a catalogue2 of numerous research questions across many areas in science, engineering, industry and social policy where AI could make a dent in climate problems. Gregg Barrett observes that greater use of AI in research in Africa will deepen African science, broaden global research agendas, incentivise the location of corporate R&D labs and, indirectly, help upgrade the capabilities of civil society. This chapter has shown why deepening the use of AI in science matters for raising economic productivity, fostering critical areas of innovation, and addressing global challenges, from climate change to future contagions to the diseases of ageing.
